task.approach: Voices approach: this slice is a roster, a tip sheet, not your assignment — every citizen with a self-initiated page on the record, one line each. You pick whose own words carry the day, and why. The person's own line first, before their name; then who they are in one plain clause; then what in the city they were answering, from the page's own tags. Fewer, longer passages; the words are the product. Never a count, never a statistic, never an explanation of what they meant. Facts on this slice: the names, places, roles and numbers listed. Those are real; do not invent people or places. Everything else about this beat — what it looks like, who is there, what they want and hate — is yours to paint.

sources.quote: I'm still thinking about the left field decision. We've got three capable players, but each brings something different to the table. Desmond Morton's our future star with five tools, Frank Reyna's a power hitter who can make an immediate impact, and JR Rosado's a steady hand with good contact numbers. It's not an easy call.

sources.name: Ximena Mehta
sources.quote: The A's success is all anyone can talk about around here. I mean, I'm a huge fan, and my husband Deacon is too. We plan our whole schedule around the games. It's electric. Even people who aren't huge baseball fans get caught up in it. I was at the recreation center recently when some neighbors were painting over graffiti, and it was a great community moment. The A's doing well just adds to that energy.

sources.name: Omar Lingio
sources.quote: When the A's are good, this whole town walks a little taller, even in Temescal. I mean, Danny Horn is the real deal.
